title: Out-of-i32 balance.json integers fail fast but carry a misleading 'no decimals' rejection message
evidence:
core/catalog.odin:1153-1157:
			di, okdi := jint_strict(bobj, "dot_interval_ticks", -1)
...			if !okdi || !okdf || !okda {
				return {"balance.json", "box", "clock keys must be integers (no decimals)"}
core/catalog.odin:1840-1842 (jint_strict_value):
	case json.Integer:
		i := i64(x)
		if i < i64(min(i32)) || i > i64(max(i32)) {
			return 0, false
core/catalog_test.odin:1082:
		{"box interval over i32 (the strict-int overflow path)", replace1(BAL_VALID, `"dot_interval_ticks": 2400`, `"dot_interval_ticks": 1099511627776`, 1), "clock keys must be integers (no decimals)"},
detail: The overflow rejection is fail-fast and safe (jint_strict_value blocks |v|>i32max, no wrap), but the boundary error conflates overflow with decimals, misdirecting content authors at the only untrusted-input boundary.
recommended_fix: Have jint_strict_value signal the reason (overflow vs wrong type) or reword the box-block message to name both causes (e.g. 'must be a strict i32 integer: no decimals, no overflow').
